title: Import Data Safely
readerIntent: Configure and run a tenant-safe import through existing Nodics contracts.
priorKnowledge: Know the source, target schema or index, mapping, tenant, and permission.
owner: Import definitions, format adapters, dataCore processors, and target schema/search services
summary: A governed import resolves trusted headers, narrows tenant scope, parses and validates input, dispatches finalized models through target services, and records run evidence.

sections.heading: Supported inputs
items: Core, init, sample, and governed local imports.
CSV, Excel, JSON, and trusted JavaScript definitions owned by active modules.
Push-based API inputs that meet the governed contract.
Named remote sources supplied by a project/provider adapter; arbitrary request URLs and credentials are forbidden.

sections.heading: Importing a file from Axis
paragraphs: A business user usually thinks of file import as one action: choose a file, validate it, and import it. Nodics intentionally splits that behind the scenes so each backend authority does only its own job.

First, Axis uploads the selected file through Media Management. Media Management validates the file type and size, stores it using the configured storage provider, calculates checksum, and creates a media record. Axis receives a media identity such as `mediaCode`; it does not receive a server filesystem path.

Second, Axis starts a governed import with that media identity by calling `POST /nodics/import/v0/media`. The request passes `mediaCode`, the selected target schema metadata, and optionally `options.validateOnly`. Import resolves the trusted media source through Media Management, creates run-local headers, stages the file into import-run-owned storage, and then either validates only or executes the existing import pipeline.
This pattern works locally and in clustered production. The browser never decides where files are stored, and the import runner never depends on a temporary folder owned by one frontend request.
sections.code:
Employee selects supplier-products.xlsx in Axis
  -> Axis uploads file to nMedia with folderCode=importSources
  -> nMedia stores bytes and returns mediaCode
  -> Axis calls POST /nodics/import/v0/media with mediaCode and selected target schema
  -> nImport builds the governed import run and generates a run-local header
  -> nImport stages the media into an import-run workspace
  -> nImport validates only or runs the existing file import pipeline
  -> Import history records success, rejected rows, counts, and recovery data

sections.heading: What must not happen
items: Axis must not pass `/tmp`, a user laptop path, a mounted NAS path, a bucket key, or a signed URL as import authority.
Import must not parse multipart browser uploads; Media Management owns media upload parsing and storage.
Media Management must not parse import rows, execute schema writes, or decide business mapping.
A project module must not create a second upload table, a second importer, or a direct persistence shortcut for one file source.
A public response must not expose absolute server paths, object-store keys, credentials, or provider internals.

sections.heading: Run flow
items: Select a trusted import definition, source, tenant, and active-module header.
Validate count, size, extension, checksum, duplicate fingerprint, and source policy.
Parse and map through format readers and data processors.
Apply interceptors, validators, access groups, and tenant narrowing.
Dispatch batches through generated schema or search services.
Record counts, diagnostics, failure, retry, rollback evidence, and finalization events.

sections.heading: Modes and identity
items: Create-only rejects existing identity.
Update-only rejects missing identity.
Upsert follows an explicit owner-approved contract.
Replace requires stronger scope, deletion, and rollback governance.
Stable source and record identities make retry and update idempotent.

sections.heading: Relationships and ordering
paragraphs: Import resolves related records through schema contracts. Parent-first ordering, deferred reference resolution, or bounded multi-pass behavior is explicit. Cross-module records still use target authority.
A missing Tenant during Enterprise import cannot be inserted directly into Profile storage.

sections.heading: Finalization
items: Commit or close the accepted run.
Reconcile indexes and search lag.
Invalidate affected caches.
Publish approved completion facts.
Start workflow or publishing only through configured ownership.
Store counts, rejects, checksums, duration, and recovery state.

sections.heading: Verify
items: Validation-only and successful runs.
Malformed, oversized, duplicate, unauthorized, cross-tenant, and partial inputs.
Batch boundaries, retries, idempotency, stop-on-failure, and cleanup.
Schema/search target contracts, cache invalidation, events, workflows, and normal-save regression.

sections.heading: Negative and recovery tests
items: Malformed source, unsupported format, excessive size, and checksum mismatch.
Invalid field, duplicate identity, missing relation, and wrong tenant.
Partial batch, provider outage, restart, resume, and duplicate delivery.
Error-threshold stop and rollback or compensation.
Index, cache, event, and finalization failure.
Reimport unchanged and changed versioned pack.
